# UCLA School Mental Health Project

> A comprehensive resource hub for implementing multi-tiered systems of support (MTSS) and addressing barriers to learning in schools through evidence-based practices and systemic change.

The UCLA School Mental Health Project, housed within the Center for Mental Health in Schools, provides implementation science guidance, professional resources, and comprehensive directories to support school mental health initiatives and student development across K-12 and transition-to-adulthood contexts.

## Key Topics

- Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS)
- Barriers to Learning
- Implementation Science
- School Mental Health
- Youth Development
- Systemic Change
- School Improvement
- Student Supports
- Adolescent Transition
- School Leadership
- Equity of Opportunity
- Professional Associations
- Resource Directory
- Child Welfare
- Learning Barriers

## Core Resources & Implementation

- [UCLA School Mental Health Project](https://smhp.psych.ucla.edu/temphome.htm): Homepage and primary entry point covering MTSS frameworks and implementation science approaches to school mental health

## Student Development & Transitions

- [Transition from Adolescence](https://smhp.psych.ucla.edu/qf/transition_from_adolescence.htm): Comprehensive guide addressing adolescent transition, dropout prevention, and college readiness support strategies

## Reference & Research Tools

- [Keywords Main Page](https://smhp.psych.ucla.edu/thesaurus.htm): Searchable keyword thesaurus for navigating school mental health topics, barriers to learning, and related resources

## Professional Networks & Associations

- [V. Matters Relevant to Addressing Barriers to Learning and Development - Associations](https://smhp.psych.ucla.edu/gateway/catvb.htm): Directory of professional associations and organizations focused on barriers to learning, youth development, and school improvement

## Publications & Announcements

- [Announcing](https://smhp.psych.ucla.edu/whatsnew/Publications.htm): Announcements of School Mental Health Project publications, research findings, and new resources
